07-1.title: Task decomposition
07-1.tldr: Either ask the model to emit a plan/todo list up front, or decompose lazily and revise; store it as structured tasks that can be marked in-progress/done.
points: Store as structured tasks with status.

07-2.title: Changing the plan mid-run
07-2.tldr: Allow plan mutation during the run — add, reorder, cancel, replace tasks — and support steering with new instructions; keep the authoritative plan separate from live state.

07-3.title: Single-step vs planning agent
07-3.tldr: Two axes: single-step vs multi-step (how many model↔tool cycles) and reactive vs planning (whether an explicit plan is kept and updated).

07-4.title: Planner-executor pattern
07-4.tldr: A planner produces the steps; one or more executors carry them out, often with a supervisor re-planning — useful when planning needs a global view and execution is parallel/specialized.

07-5.title: State across steps
07-5.tldr: A state object threaded through (or held per session) that each step reads/writes; conversation history is usually separate from working state; persist via checkpoints.
points: Separate conversation history from task state.

07-6.title: Pause and resume an agent
07-6.tldr: Pause needs a durable checkpoint at a safe boundary or a first-class interrupt that unwinds the run preserving state; resume reloads the checkpoint or replays the suspended step.

07-7.title: Human-in-the-loop approval
07-7.tldr: Route sensitive steps through a permission check returning allow/ask/deny, pause on ask, surface a confirm payload, resume with the decision, and remember/persist rules; fail closed on unknown.
points: Pause on ask; resume with the decision.

07-8.title: Short vs long-term memory
07-8.tldr: Short-term is the live working context (recent turns, task state) for the next call; long-term is durable cross-session knowledge retrieved on demand.
points: Long-term is retrieved into the turn.

07-9.title: What to store vs discard
07-9.tldr: Keep durable, reused, preference-like, decision-relevant facts; discard transient chatter and stale/contradicted entries — usually extract candidates with an LLM, then dedupe/resolve.

07-10.title: Bounding memory growth
07-10.tldr: Bound on multiple axes: hard-drop/truncate oldest context, offload large blobs, compact old tool results, summarize/archive, and cap stored long-term entries.
points: Offload large blobs; compact tool results.

07-11.title: Summarizing history safely
07-11.tldr: Keep recent turns verbatim; summarize older turns into a structured note (goal, decisions, files/state, open tasks, next step) rather than free prose; re-inject durable state.

07-12.title: Planner–executor pattern
07-12.tldr: A planner breaks a complex request into subtasks; one or more executors carry each out; results are combined into a final response.

07-13.title: Critic or reflection loop
07-13.tldr: A self-check before returning: the primary agent drafts, a critic reviews against the request or rules, and the primary revises if it fails.

07-14.title: Memory-augmented agent
07-14.tldr: Context across sessions: short-term is the active window; long-term is a store of past interactions; retrieval decides what long-term memory returns.

07-15.title: Memory contamination and targeted invalidation
07-15.tldr: Wrong facts written to memory compound across sessions; prevent via write gating, and fix via targeted overwrite — not full wipes.
points: Prevention: write only from verified outputs; tag with provenance.
Fix: memory_update(id) for targeted overwrite; memory_delete_by_category for broad wipe.
Gap: no confidence gate before write, no versioning, no audit loop.
